meta.name: MarketMove
meta.description: Architectural roadmap explorer for the Western AI MarketMove project.
meta.status: Planning visualization — not a live delivery tracker
meta.sourcePolicy: Revised November 7, 2026 roadmap controls sprint dates; older foundation outline controls project architecture and scientific constraints.

stages.title: Source signals
stages.subtitle: What the system knows
stages.summary: Raw inputs. Nothing here is computed by the team: these sources are loaded, profiled and audited before anything is built on them.

stages.title: Data foundations
stages.subtitle: Make time and identity trustworthy
stages.summary: Turns raw sources into a dataset with trustworthy identity (which outcome token?) and time (what was really known at T?). Holds the first feasibility gate.

stages.title: Prediction engine
stages.subtitle: Turn signals into evidence
stages.summary: Features, baselines, the fused model and the experiments that decide whether news adds anything beyond the market itself.

stages.title: Product & evidence
stages.subtitle: Make results inspectable
stages.summary: Serves the frozen model and makes results inspectable: prediction and replay APIs, Live Analyze, Historical Replay, the evidence dashboard and the paper.

sprints.title: Prove the join
sprints.summary: Confirm source schemas, token-level matching and whether trustworthy six-hour labels are possible before investing in models.
sprints.note: Go / no-go: continue only if source join and historical labels look viable.

sprints.title: Ship dataset v0
sprints.summary: Make raw-to-clean data reproducible, establish leakage-safe market-only baseline, and decide whether the dataset is viable.

deliverables.title: Reproducible Parquet v0

sprints.title: First fused loop
sprints.summary: Complete a tiny end-to-end market + news → prediction → actual comparison, with all committed work finished by December 9.
sprints.note: December 10–22 is protected exam time. Do not assign normal sprint velocity.

deliverables.title: Small verified fixture

nodes.title: PolyBench
nodes.subtitle: Historical market snapshots
nodes.description: Market definitions, snapshot probability, token IDs and candidate news context captured at historical time T.
nodes.risk: News may be retrospective, not truly available at T

guide.definition: A historical benchmark of prediction-market snapshots. Each record captures a market at time T: question, description, resolution criteria, probability, timestamp, outcome-token IDs (clob_token_ids), news context and snapshot order-book data.
guide.why: It supplies the “what was known at T” half of every training example, and the token IDs that make a precise join possible.
responsibilities: Load and profile the schema, timestamps, market metadata, news fields and token identifiers.
Flag duplicate records, missing data and fields whose timing is uncertain.
Produce a normalized sample and a written list of uncertainties that could block training.
Hand normalized clob_token_ids to the outcome-token join.
resources: Python · pandas / Polars for loading and profiling

nodes.title: Polymarket-v1
nodes.subtitle: Trades & realized prices
nodes.description: Trade-level history used to reconstruct market state before T and observed outcomes near T+6h.
nodes.inputs: Asset ID, timestamp, trade price and size
nodes.outputs: Historic prices, volume and future-label observations
nodes.risk: Sparse trades and ambiguous outcome mappings

guide.definition: Polymarket-v1 trade history: token / asset ID, condition ID, timestamp, trade price, trade size, market slug and outcome.
guide.why: Trades are the only record of the market’s path: the price history before T (features) and the observed price near T + 6h (labels).
responsibilities: Confirm which columns support historical price and volume reconstruction.
Document how a single trade maps to a specific market outcome (YES / NO token).
Provide normalized trades keyed by asset_id for the join and the label builder.
Expose sparsity, so illiquid markets are filtered rather than guessed.
resources: Python · pandas / Polars; Parquet for normalized trades

nodes.title: News at time T
nodes.subtitle: Timestamped headlines
nodes.description: News text and publication-time provenance; only information available at prediction time may enter features.
nodes.inputs: News text, publication time, market proposition
nodes.risk: Retrospective summaries and later publication updates

guide.definition: The news text attached to a market, with when it was published and how it relates to the market proposition. At serving time, it is the headline the user enters.
guide.why: News is the variable under test. If a headline was not really available at T, any lift it shows is leakage, not signal.
responsibilities: Separate genuinely timestamped headlines from context written or updated after the fact.
Classify timestamp reliability and attach a flag to each headline.
Pass only eligible headlines into the dataset and the NLP pipeline.
Document which news fields are safe to use at T.
resources: Manual sample review of timestamp reliability

nodes.title: Live Polymarket
nodes.subtitle: Market state endpoints
nodes.description: Future live connector for market selection, price and supported history. Not the same as historical training data.
nodes.risk: API rate limits and training/serving parity

guide.definition: A planned adapter to Polymarket’s live interfaces for market search, current price and whatever history they support.
guide.why: Live Analyze needs a current market state, and it must be built the same way as the training features or the prediction is meaningless.
responsibilities: Look up supported markets; return current probability and recent history.
Document rate limits and fields that are unavailable live.
Map live fields onto the training feature definitions (training / serving parity).
Fail clearly, so the demo can fall back to Historical Replay.
resources: Polymarket market, price and history interfaces where available

nodes.title: Contracts & tooling
nodes.subtitle: Schema · tests · CI
nodes.description: UTC timestamps, normalized identifiers, percent-point labels, project setup and shared API contracts.
nodes.risk: Inconsistent units or hidden assumptions

guide.definition: The shared rules and scaffolding every component builds against: repository, dependencies, tests, linting, CI, data schemas and conventions.
guide.why: Five people build separate pieces; contracts are what make them fit. Units, IDs or timestamps that disagree silently break everything downstream.
responsibilities: Standardize UTC timestamps, normalized token IDs, probability units and percentage-point deltas (never relative percent).
Define the fields for snapshots, normalized trades, labels, market features, news features and predictions.
Define the combined market + news input shape without letting labels leak in as predictors.
Keep interfaces and model inputs / outputs documented across the exam break.
resources: DATA_SCHEMA.md with sample JSON / Parquet schemas
Python project structure, test setup, linting and CI
guide.note: No arrows on the map by design: it is cross-cutting, and every component depends on it.

nodes.title: Outcome-token join
nodes.subtitle: clob_token_ids ↔ asset_id
nodes.description: Validate token-level join coverage and YES/NO mappings. No silent fuzzy-text fallback.
nodes.risk: Unmatched, duplicate or ambiguous token IDs

guide.definition: The bridge between the two historical datasets: PolyBench clob_token_ids matched to Polymarket-v1 asset_id, at the level of individual outcome tokens.
guide.why: It is the first feasibility question. If the join fails or covers too few independent events, the project must be reformulated before any modelling.
responsibilities: Normalize token IDs and match each snapshot to the trades of exactly that outcome.
Resolve YES / NO mapping and duplicate matches explicitly.
Never fall back silently to fuzzy matching on market names or questions.
Produce a coverage funnel (match counts, rejected records, hand-checked examples), then turn the pilot into a repeatable, tested pipeline.
resources: Python · pandas / Polars; tests for unmatched and ambiguous tokens
Planning thresholds: ≥ 5,000 examples and ≥ 1,000 events is strong; < 1,000 trustworthy examples means reformulate

nodes.title: 6h label builder
nodes.subtitle: Future state at T + 6h
nodes.description: Reconstruct p(T+6h) with documented time windows, staleness and trade quality checks.
nodes.outputs: Delta in percentage points + label quality
nodes.risk: Do not leak the future into model features

guide.definition: The function that produces the target: the market’s probability around T + 6h, and the move from T in percentage points.
guide.why: Markets rarely trade exactly at T + 6h. Without a careful, documented label the model learns from noise, or from the future.
responsibilities: Find the outcome price near T + 6h: nearest valid trade within a tolerance, VWAP or volume-weighted median.
Return p_t, p_t6h, the delta, observed timestamp, offset, trade count and a label-quality rating.
Reject stale, illiquid or unsupported outcomes explicitly.
Support 1h / 24h horizon ablations while keeping six hours primary.
resources: Configurable timestamp tolerances and label methods

nodes.title: Training dataset
nodes.subtitle: Curated Parquet + manifests
nodes.description: One reproducible example per valid snapshot with valid features, event grouping, outcomes and source provenance.
nodes.outputs: Deterministic training data and quality report
nodes.risk: Sample size and event coverage are unproven

guide.definition: The curated, versioned Parquet dataset: one example per valid snapshot, with market state, eligible news, the six-hour label, event grouping and source provenance.
guide.why: Every model, metric, replay fixture and paper table is built from it. If it cannot be rebuilt identically, no result can be trusted.
responsibilities: Combine valid snapshots, labels and news metadata, with event IDs for event-disjoint splits.
Report raw-to-clean coverage, independent events, missingness, label quality and exclusions.
Build deterministically from a versioned manifest, so another developer regenerates the same data.
Export small verified fixtures and Historical Replay examples, keeping outcomes out of prediction inputs.
resources: Paper: dataset and preprocessing methods section

nodes.title: Prospective logger
nodes.subtitle: Pre-outcome observations
nodes.description: Capture prediction-time data before outcomes are known; append later observations separately.
nodes.inputs: Immutable T snapshot + future observed state
nodes.risk: Never rewrite historical inputs with future values

guide.definition: A collector that records predictions and their inputs before outcomes are known, then attaches the later +1h / +6h / +24h observations as separate records.
guide.why: It yields a clean evaluation set without historical-timestamp doubts or LLM contamination: the outcome did not exist when the prediction was made.
responsibilities: Store immutable prediction-time inputs: headline, market, market state and model prediction.
Append later observed states as separate records; never overwrite inputs.
Track failures and missing observations.
Feed prospective records back to the Evaluation lab.
guide.note: Its sources (live market state and served predictions) are not drawn as edges; only its feedback into evaluation is.

nodes.title: Market features
nodes.subtitle: Momentum · volatility · volume
nodes.description: Generate only reconstructible market signals using trade history at or before T.
nodes.risk: Missing order-book or liquidity features must remain missing

guide.definition: Market-state signals built only from trades at or before T: price at T, momentum windows, volatility and recent volume.
guide.why: They form the Market Only baseline, the bar news has to beat, and half of the fused model’s input.
responsibilities: Compute price at T, available momentum windows (e.g. 15 min, 1 h, 6 h), volatility and recent volume.
Test that no feature uses a trade after T.
Keep order-book, spread and liquidity features missing and documented when they cannot be reconstructed; never fabricate them.
Emit a vector aligned by example ID.

nodes.title: News semantics
nodes.subtitle: Embeddings · relevance · stance
nodes.description: Frozen encoder, proposition relevance and optional stance features with verified publication times.
nodes.risk: No contaminated future-aware text reasoning

guide.definition: The NLP pipeline: a pinned, frozen pretrained text encoder that embeds the headline and the market proposition, plus relevance and optional stance features.
guide.why: It turns text into model inputs without letting a modern model’s hindsight about historical events contaminate them.
responsibilities: Relevance: does the headline concern this market? (embedding similarity).
Stance: does it support YES, contradict YES or stay neutral? (frozen NLI, optional).
Batch, cache and version outputs with consistent columns and explicit handling of missing text.
Leave stance out by default if manual review finds it unreliable.
resources: Manual inspection set (≥ 30 examples) for stance accuracy

nodes.title: Baseline models
nodes.subtitle: Trivial / market / news
nodes.description: Comparable baseline models on the same eligible examples and event-disjoint splits.
nodes.inputs: Market features, news features, T+6h labels
nodes.risk: Training/test leakage and class imbalance

guide.definition: The comparison models: Trivial (always FLAT / no significant move), Market Only (XGBoost) and News Only.
guide.why: Without them there is no way to tell whether the fused model learned anything that news adds.
responsibilities: Use event-disjoint train / validation / test splits, so related markets never cross the boundary.
Train on exactly the same eligible examples as the fused model.
Choose the significant-move threshold on training data only; keep the test set untouched.
Report significant-move AUPRC, direction Macro F1, class balance and split details.
resources: Event IDs from the training dataset

nodes.title: Fused predictor
nodes.subtitle: Late-fusion XGBoost
nodes.description: Fuse market and news features to estimate significant-move probability and direction; magnitude only if validated.
nodes.risk: News lift is a hypothesis, not a guaranteed result

guide.definition: The core predictor: late-fusion XGBoost over the concatenated market and news feature vectors.
guide.why: It tests the central hypothesis, that news carries information beyond what the market already shows.
responsibilities: Predict the probability of a significant move and the direction (UP / FLAT / DOWN) over six hours.
Add magnitude with an uncertainty range only if evaluation supports it.
Save predictions, configuration and metrics for every run.
Stay simple: neural or cross-encoder fusion only after this shows real signal.
resources: XGBoost; PyTorch reserved for later neural experiments

nodes.title: Evaluation lab
nodes.subtitle: Ablations · calibration
nodes.description: Compare Market Only, News Only and Market + News, horizons and robustness under event-aware splits.
nodes.outputs: AUPRC, macro F1, robustness and calibrated evidence
nodes.risk: Prevent cherry-picking thresholds and results

guide.definition: Where every claim is tested: ablations, horizons, robustness, calibration and the final experimental report.
guide.why: It decides what the project can honestly say. Everything in the dashboard and paper must trace back to its saved outputs.
responsibilities: Compare Trivial, Market Only, News Only and Market + News on the same examples and splits.
Run 1h / 6h / 24h horizon ablations and error analysis by topic, liquidity and label quality.
Assess calibration on validation data and report reliability on held-out data.
Use fixed seeds, versioned inputs and machine-readable metrics; reconcile every published number.
resources: Metrics: AUPRC, AUROC, precision / recall, Macro F1, magnitude MAE, calibration

nodes.title: Model artifacts
nodes.subtitle: Versioned inference contract
nodes.description: Freeze model, encoder, preprocessing configuration and threshold with reproducible API parity.
nodes.risk: Mismatch between offline and deployed predictions

guide.definition: The frozen, versioned inference package: model weights, encoder version, preprocessing, feature schema, threshold and calibration.
guide.why: It guarantees that what was evaluated offline is exactly what the API and Replay serve.
responsibilities: Export the model and preprocessing behind a callable predict function with an explicit schema.
Test that predictions are identical after reloading.
Pin every artifact at the research freeze.
Verify parity between offline evaluation and API results.

nodes.title: Inference API
nodes.subtitle: FastAPI prediction service
nodes.description: Validate and serve six-hour model predictions with version metadata and safe handling of unavailable features.
nodes.risk: No unvalidated model outputs should be presented as facts

guide.definition: A FastAPI service that validates inputs and serves typed six-hour predictions.
guide.why: It is the single door between the model and the product, and decides what users are allowed to see.
responsibilities: Accept the documented feature inputs; return the supported outputs with model-version metadata.
Handle unavailable features safely and return useful errors.
Never present an unvalidated output as fact.
Be tested for model loading, latency, invalid input and external outages, with an offline fallback.

nodes.title: Replay service
nodes.subtitle: Historical T / T+6h endpoints
nodes.description: Return replay snapshots while withholding future outcomes until the reveal interaction.
nodes.risk: Future-label leakage into initial inference

guide.definition: Backend endpoints for Historical Replay: fetch the snapshot at T, generate a prediction, then reveal the observed T + 6h outcome.
guide.why: Replay is only convincing if the future is genuinely hidden when the prediction is made.
responsibilities: Serve a historical snapshot containing only information available at T.
Run inference through the same model package as the live API.
Withhold the later outcome until the reveal request.
Prove with tests that hidden future data cannot reach inference.
resources: Replay fixtures from the training dataset

nodes.title: Live Analyze
nodes.subtitle: Market + headline UI
nodes.description: User chooses a market, enters news and explores a six-hour prediction and its caveats.
nodes.risk: No automatic trading or guaranteed returns

guide.definition: The main product flow: choose a supported market, enter a headline, see the six-hour forecast and its caveats.
guide.why: It is the experience the project statement describes, and shows what MarketMove is for.
responsibilities: Search and select a supported market; show its current probability.
Accept a headline and request a prediction from the real API.
Display only outputs the model supports, with uncertainty and caveats.
Make clear it is not trading advice or automated betting.
resources: React / Next.js / Tailwind + a charting library (recommended, not locked)
guide.note: A live extra: when capacity shrinks, Historical Replay and evaluation come first.

nodes.title: Historical Replay
nodes.subtitle: Freeze · forecast · reveal
nodes.description: Interactive prediction-versus-reality story with true time boundaries and a reliable cached demo mode.
nodes.risk: Demo values must be real or explicitly illustrative

guide.definition: An interactive prediction-versus-reality story: freeze a market at T, forecast, fast-forward six hours, reveal what actually happened.
guide.why: It turns “an AI says this might move the market” into “here is what it predicted, and here is what happened”, and it is the reliable demo mode.
responsibilities: Show market selection, the historical snapshot and the prediction.
Run the six-hour fast-forward and reveal, marking direction and significance correct or incorrect.
Work from cached examples and local artifacts if live services fail.
Use real values, or label illustrative ones explicitly.
resources: Frontend + charting for the price-path animation
Cached replay fixtures and local model artifacts

nodes.title: Evidence dashboard
nodes.subtitle: Baseline comparison
nodes.description: Display sample sizes, saved evaluation results, model versions and limitations without implying unsupported lift.
nodes.risk: No fabricated performance metrics

guide.definition: The “Does MarketMove actually work?” page.
guide.why: It shows the evidence as it is, so viewers can judge the claims for themselves.
responsibilities: Visualize saved Market Only, News Only and Market + News metrics.
Show sample counts, model versions and limitations next to every number.
Never imply stronger evidence than was evaluated.
Read from saved experiment outputs, not hand-typed numbers.

nodes.title: Paper & CUCAI
nodes.subtitle: Research freeze · showcase
nodes.description: Paper, methods, reproducible artifacts, presentation, demo reliability and CUCAI readiness.
nodes.outputs: Reviewable research story and event-ready demo
nodes.risk: Submission and event dates are provisional

guide.definition: The finish line: research paper, reproducible artifacts, presentation, demo reliability and CUCAI Q&A.
guide.why: It is where the work is judged; every upstream component contributes a section, a figure or a demo.
responsibilities: Run the research-freeze review: approve dataset and model versions, experiments, figures and known limitations.
Assemble the paper; reconcile terminology, figures, citations and claims.
Rehearse the demo and the technical Q&A.
Confirm the paper deadline and event dates, which are still provisional.
resources: Methods sections from the data, model, evaluation and deployment owners
Demo script, backup recordings and slides

edges.carries: Trade asset_id values to match against
p(T + 6h), delta in points, label-quality fields
Per-example price history at or before T
Example IDs to align text features to
Baseline predictions on the same examples
Validated model choice, threshold and calibration
The same package, for replay-safe inference
Replay fixtures: state at T + withheld outcome
Current state of the selected market
Snapshot and prediction, then the reveal
Saved metrics, sample sizes and model versions
Comparison figures for the paper and talk

tickets.title: Initialize development repository
tickets.description: Create the Python project structure, dependencies, test setup, linting, and basic CI.
tickets.acceptance: A new developer can clone, install dependencies, run a sample script, and pass the repository's initial automated checks.

tickets.title: Define shared data and ML contracts
tickets.description: Establish the expected fields for snapshots, normalized trades, labels, market features, news features, and predictions. Standardize UTC timestamps, token IDs, probability units, and percentage-point deltas.
tickets.acceptance: `DATA_SCHEMA.md` is reviewed by the team, and sample JSON/Parquet schemas are available to implement against.

tickets.title: Explore and profile PolyBench
tickets.description: Write a loader and inspect schema, timestamps, market metadata, news fields, token identifiers, duplicate records, and missing data.
tickets.acceptance: Produce a dataset profile, a normalized sample, and a written list of uncertainties that could block training.

tickets.acceptance: Provide a normalized trades sample and document how a trade relates to a specific market outcome.

tickets.acceptance: Review a representative sample, classify timestamp reliability, and document which news fields are safe to use at T.

tickets.acceptance: Build the label function with configurable timestamp tolerances and label methods. Output future price, six-hour delta, observed timestamp, and quality fields. Reject stale/unsupported outcomes explicitly.

tickets.title: Export training dataset v0 and quality report

tickets.acceptance: Combine valid snapshots, labels, and news metadata into Parquet. Report raw-to-clean coverage, number of independent events, missingness, label quality, and exclusions.

tickets.acceptance: Generate price at T, available momentum windows, volatility, and recent volume. Test that no feature uses a trade after T. Document unavailable features rather than fabricating liquidity/order-book values.

tickets.title: Implement baseline training and evaluation

tickets.acceptance: Create event-disjoint train/validation/test splits, trivial baselines, and a first market-only XGBoost model. Output significant-move AUPRC, direction Macro F1 where feasible, class balance, and split details.

tickets.acceptance: Encode eligible headlines and market propositions using a pinned pretrained encoder. Output vectors, similarity/relevance features, and example comparisons.

tickets.acceptance: Define the shared input shape for market + news modeling. Demonstrate merging features by example ID without accidentally including outcome labels as predictors.

tickets.acceptance: Record dataset coverage, baseline results, known risks, the selected significance threshold, and a proceed/reformulate recommendation.

tickets.acceptance: Export a small, fixed set of clean examples with market state, eligible news, labels, and consistent IDs. Include a dataset manifest.

tickets.title: Generate aligned semantic features

tickets.title: Train first fused model
tickets.description: Combine market and news features in a simple XGBoost model. Produce predictions on a small held-out set. Save the runnable experiment configuration.
tickets.acceptance: Combine market and news features in a simple XGBoost model. Produce predictions on a small held-out set. Save the runnable experiment configuration.

tickets.title: Compare first model variants
tickets.description: Compare trivial, Market Only, News Only, and Market + News on the same valid examples and evaluation split. Record differences without claiming significance from a small pilot.
tickets.acceptance: Compare trivial, Market Only, News Only, and Market + News on the same valid examples and evaluation split. Record differences without claiming significance from a small pilot.

tickets.title: Document pre-exam technical status
tickets.description: Record completed work, known bugs, blocked items, and the first tasks for January. Ensure all interfaces and model inputs/outputs are documented.
tickets.acceptance: Record completed work, known bugs, blocked items, and the first tasks for January. Ensure all interfaces and model inputs/outputs are documented.

tickets.title: Finalize training dataset v1
tickets.description: Produce a deterministic dataset build with validated labels, quality filters, event identifiers, and a versioned manifest. Another developer must be able to regenerate the same dataset.
tickets.acceptance: Produce a deterministic dataset build with validated labels, quality filters, event identifiers, and a versioned manifest. Another developer must be able to regenerate the same dataset.

tickets.title: Implement batch news-feature extraction
tickets.description: Convert the prototype into a reusable pipeline for embeddings and relevance. Support batching, caching, pinned encoder versions, missing text, and consistent output columns.
tickets.acceptance: Convert the prototype into a reusable pipeline for embeddings and relevance. Support batching, caching, pinned encoder versions, missing text, and consistent output columns.

tickets.title: Evaluate proposition-stance features
tickets.description: Test a frozen NLI model or other suitable approach for supports-YES, contradicts-YES, and neutral classifications. Manually inspect at least 30 suitable examples. Document accuracy concerns; don't include unreliable stance features by default.
tickets.acceptance: Test a frozen NLI model or other suitable approach for supports-YES, contradicts-YES, and neutral classifications. Manually inspect at least 30 suitable examples. Document accuracy concerns; don't include unreliable stance features by default.

tickets.title: Build reproducible experiment runner
tickets.description: Create a training/evaluation command with fixed seeds, configurations, event-disjoint splits, versioned inputs, and machine-readable metric outputs.
tickets.acceptance: Create a training/evaluation command with fixed seeds, configurations, event-disjoint splits, versioned inputs, and machine-readable metric outputs.

tickets.title: Establish official baseline comparisons
tickets.description: Re-run trivial, market-only, and news-only baselines on the same eligible examples. Choose the significant-move threshold using training data only and preserve the untouched test set.
tickets.acceptance: Re-run trivial, market-only, and news-only baselines on the same eligible examples. Choose the significant-move threshold using training data only and preserve the untouched test set.

tickets.title: Train the complete fused model
tickets.description: Train a model combining market state and news features. Implement six-hour significant-move and direction prediction, using simple late fusion first. Save validation predictions, configuration, and metrics.
tickets.acceptance: Train a model combining market state and news features. Implement six-hour significant-move and direction prediction, using simple late fusion first. Save validation predictions, configuration, and metrics.

tickets.title: Package reproducible inference
tickets.description: Export the trained model and preprocessing configuration. Provide a callable prediction function with an explicit schema and a test showing consistent predictions after reloading.
tickets.acceptance: Export the trained model and preprocessing configuration. Provide a callable prediction function with an explicit schema and a test showing consistent predictions after reloading.

tickets.title: Review first meaningful results
tickets.description: Review data quality, baseline comparison, fused-model results, implementation completeness, and experiment risks. Decide which improvements are worth pursuing before February.
tickets.acceptance: Review data quality, baseline comparison, fused-model results, implementation completeness, and experiment risks. Decide which improvements are worth pursuing before February.

tickets.title: Generate Historical Replay fixtures
tickets.description: Create reproducible historical examples containing the market state at T, eligible news, a model prediction, and the observed outcome at T+6h. Keep future outcome data outside the prediction input.
tickets.acceptance: Create reproducible historical examples containing the market state at T, eligible news, a model prediction, and the observed outcome at T+6h. Keep future outcome data outside the prediction input.

tickets.title: Automate prospective prediction collection
tickets.description: Build on the initial snapshot-logging procedure. Store immutable prediction-time inputs and later attach observed outcomes as separate records. Track failures and missing observations.
tickets.acceptance: Build on the initial snapshot-logging procedure. Store immutable prediction-time inputs and later attach observed outcomes as separate records. Track failures and missing observations.

tickets.title: Run prediction-horizon ablation
tickets.description: Compare 1h, 6h, and 24h predictions where valid labels exist. Apply comparable splits, report sample coverage, and explain differences in performance. Keep six hours as the primary target unless formally changed.
tickets.acceptance: Compare 1h, 6h, and 24h predictions where valid labels exist. Apply comparable splits, report sample coverage, and explain differences in performance. Keep six hours as the primary target unless formally changed.

tickets.title: Perform error and robustness analysis
tickets.description: Evaluate model behavior by market topic, liquidity, label quality, and other meaningful groups. Identify systematic failures and differences from the market-only baseline.
tickets.acceptance: Evaluate model behavior by market topic, liquidity, label quality, and other meaningful groups. Identify systematic failures and differences from the market-only baseline.

tickets.title: Build model inference API
tickets.description: Implement a FastAPI endpoint that accepts the documented feature inputs and returns available prediction outputs. Add validation tests, version metadata, and useful error responses.
tickets.acceptance: Implement a FastAPI endpoint that accepts the documented feature inputs and returns available prediction outputs. Add validation tests, version metadata, and useful error responses.

tickets.title: Build Historical Replay service
tickets.description: Provide endpoints for retrieving a historical snapshot, generating a prediction, and revealing the later outcome. Test that hidden future information cannot enter model inference.
tickets.acceptance: Provide endpoints for retrieving a historical snapshot, generating a prediction, and revealing the later outcome. Test that hidden future information cannot enter model inference.

tickets.title: Implement Historical Replay interface
tickets.description: Build market selection, historical snapshot display, prediction results, and the six-hour fast-forward interaction. Integrate with real replay endpoints and handle missing data.
tickets.acceptance: Build market selection, historical snapshot display, prediction results, and the six-hour fast-forward interaction. Integrate with real replay endpoints and handle missing data.

tickets.title: Build basic evaluation dashboard
tickets.description: Visualize saved Market Only, News Only, and Market + News metrics. Include sample counts and model versions so the dashboard cannot accidentally imply stronger evidence than was evaluated.
tickets.acceptance: Visualize saved Market Only, News Only, and Market + News metrics. Include sample counts and model versions so the dashboard cannot accidentally imply stronger evidence than was evaluated.

tickets.title: Evaluate confidence calibration
tickets.description: Assess predicted significant-move probabilities against observed frequencies. Evaluate a suitable calibration method using validation data and report reliability on held-out data.
tickets.acceptance: Assess predicted significant-move probabilities against observed frequencies. Evaluate a suitable calibration method using validation data and report reliability on held-out data.

tickets.title: Produce final experimental report
tickets.description: Produce final comparison tables, ablations, robustness figures, sample sizes, and limitations. Document which model claims are supported by evidence and which are not.
tickets.acceptance: Produce final comparison tables, ablations, robustness figures, sample sizes, and limitations. Document which model claims are supported by evidence and which are not.

tickets.title: Freeze dataset and audit reproducibility
tickets.description: Lock the final dataset version, source provenance, quality report, and generation configuration. Independently verify that core dataset outputs can be rebuilt.
tickets.acceptance: Lock the final dataset version, source provenance, quality report, and generation configuration. Independently verify that core dataset outputs can be rebuilt.

tickets.title: Implement live market integration
tickets.description: Create an adapter for supported Polymarket market search, current price, and historical state APIs. Document rate limits, unavailable fields, and how live features match training features.
tickets.acceptance: Create an adapter for supported Polymarket market search, current price, and historical state APIs. Document rate limits, unavailable fields, and how live features match training features.

tickets.title: Freeze model and inference artifacts

tickets.acceptance: Pin model weights, preprocessing, feature schema, threshold, calibration, and configurations. Verify inference parity between offline evaluation and API results.

tickets.title: Implement Live Analyze interface
tickets.description: Allow users to select a supported market, enter news, and request a prediction. Display the current market probability and supported outputs using real API responses.
tickets.acceptance: Allow users to select a supported market, enter news, and request a prediction. Display the current market probability and supported outputs using real API responses.

tickets.title: Add reliable demo fallback

tickets.acceptance: Make Historical Replay usable with cached historical examples and local model artifacts if the live market service is unavailable.

tickets.title: Conduct final research freeze review
tickets.description: Approve dataset/model versions, experiments, paper figures, known limitations, and unresolved noncritical issues. Record the frozen research configuration.
tickets.acceptance: Approve dataset/model versions, experiments, paper figures, known limitations, and unresolved noncritical issues. Record the frozen research configuration.

tickets.acceptance: Document data sources, joins, label reconstruction, feature availability, filtering, and dataset limitations. Provide the data coverage diagram and tables.

tickets.title: Write experiments and results
tickets.description: Write evaluation methodology, baselines, ablations, confidence analysis, primary findings, and limitations. Reconcile all reported numbers with saved experiment files.
tickets.acceptance: Write evaluation methodology, baselines, ablations, confidence analysis, primary findings, and limitations. Reconcile all reported numbers with saved experiment files.

tickets.title: Write model methodology

tickets.acceptance: Document feature fusion, model architecture, training configurations, prediction tasks, and inference. Explain why the chosen methods were appropriate.

tickets.acceptance: Document installation, startup, API behavior, dependencies, configuration, failure handling, and offline fallback procedures.

tickets.acceptance: Refine the frontend, charts, labels, loading states, and walkthrough. Produce a recorded backup and verify the demo on the presentation device.

tickets.acceptance: Assemble all sections, reconcile terminology and figures, manage reviews, verify citations and claims, and submit by the confirmed deadline.

tickets.acceptance: Rebuild the dataset and representative predictions from repository instructions. Confirm that required files, configurations, and documentation are accessible.

tickets.acceptance: Test model loading, API failures, latency, invalid inputs, external service unavailability, and Historical Replay fallback.

tickets.acceptance: Complete the demo script, verify all interaction flows, and prepare backup screenshots or recordings.

principles.title: Feasibility before complexity
principles.body: Validate the PolyBench → Polymarket-v1 join and labels before training a fused model.

principles.title: Information must exist at T
principles.body: No future prices, later news, final resolutions or hindsight labels may enter model features.

principles.title: Evidence before claims
principles.body: Test Market Only vs. News Only vs. Market + News on held-out events; do not assume news adds value.

principles.title: Research first, polish second
principles.body: When capacity shrinks, protect data correctness, evaluation and Historical Replay ahead of live extras.

limitations.title: Dataset join unverified
limitations.body: PolyBench clob_token_ids ↔ Polymarket-v1 asset_id coverage and mapping reliability are not yet measured.

limitations.title: Timestamp trust
limitations.body: Historical news may be retrospective; true availability at T must be audited before any feature is used.

limitations.title: Event leakage
limitations.body: Correlated markets from the same event must never straddle train and test splits.

limitations.title: No guaranteed news lift
limitations.body: Market + News beating Market Only is the research question, not an assumed result.

limitations.title: Magnitude is conditional
limitations.body: Primary output is significant move + direction at T+6h; magnitude is shown only if evaluation supports it.

limitations.title: Research dates provisional
limitations.body: The ≈ Feb 27 paper target and early-March CUCAI showcase need confirmation; only the Feb 12 freeze is an internal fixed target.
